title: Acute and Time-Dependent Effects of Eccentric Exercise on Neuromuscular Performance and Movement Control: A Randomized Three-Arm Study
summary:
During everyday and sporting activities, muscles work by resisting a load while lengthening. This is known as eccentric muscle action. This type of exercise allows muscles to produce high forces with relatively low energy demands. However, little is known about how rest periods between exercise sets affect maximal muscle strength and movement control immediately after exercise and during subsequent recovery.

Study 1 | Physical Performance: This study investigates how different rest periods during eccentric exercise affect maximal leg-press force, jump performance, and muscle activity, and how these responses change during recovery.

Study 2 | Movement Control: This study investigates how rest duration affects stability during jump landings, walking patterns, and the ability to restore stable walking following unexpected changes in treadmill speed.

The study will include 60 healthy, physically active adults aged 18–35 years. Participants will be randomly assigned to one of three groups. All participants will complete a single exercise session on a leg-press machine consisting of eight sets of ten repetitions. Two groups will perform eccentric exercise with either 10 or 60 seconds of rest between sets. The third group will perform concentric exercise with 60 seconds of rest between sets. Assessments will take place before, immediately after, and 60 minutes, and 24 hours after exercise.

interventions.name: Eccentric isokinetic leg press: 8 × 10 repetitions at 100 mm/s and 70% of the individual maximal eccentric force–position curve; 10 s inter-set rest.
Eccentric isokinetic leg press: 8 × 10 repetitions at 100 mm/s and 70% of the individual maximal eccentric force–position curve; 60 s inter-set rest.
Concentric isokinetic leg press: 8 × 10 repetitions at 200 mm/s with maximal voluntary effort; 70% of the individual maximal eccentric force–position curve as a visual reference; 60 s inter-set rest.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Healthy adults aged 18–35 years.
- McKay Tier 1–2 training level (recreational or club-level athletes).
- Regular physical activity: ≥150 min of moderate or ≥75 min of vigorous physical activity per week, plus muscle-strengthening activities on ≥2 days per week.
- Medical eligibility confirmed by standardized health screening and voluntary written informed consent.
Exclusion criteria:
- Physical activity below the specified minimum requirements or McKay Tier 0 or Tier 3–5 training level (national/international competitive athletes).
- Acute or previous severe injuries of the lower extremities.
- Medical conditions, symptoms, or contraindications preventing the safe performance of maximal strength, jump, or treadmill tests.
- Reduced exercise tolerance, relevant balance or gait impairments, or acute illness.
